# dsh-godot — Godot capability family for DeepSeek Harness
English | 中文
A family of Godot Engine plugins for the DeepSeek Harness agent harness: headless project tooling, G
DScript semantic navigation, a scripted debugger, and a visual sandbox for a running game. Maintaine
d as an independent repository; the packages build inside the harness monorepo workspace.
## Summary
Point the agent at a Godot project and it can validate scripts, run a scene headless, format GDScrip
t, inspect project files, debug a scripted run, and drive a running game it can see. One optional bu
ndle installs the whole family; `dsh-base` and `dsh-web-app` stay free of Godot rows, so a project t
hat never uses Godot pays nothing. Each package declares its own host requirement — a Godot 4.2+ bin
ary, and optionally gdformat — and reports a missing executable at call time, never at load.
## Features
| Package | Role | DSH seam |
| `bundle-godot/` | **Optional capability bundle**: installs the five packages below as one profile

bundle; Godot is not part of `dsh-base` or `dsh-web-app` | `dsh.bundle.patch` |
| `tool-godot/` | He
adless CLI tools: `godot_validate`, `godot_run_scene`, `godot_format`, `godot_inspect`, `godot_edito

r_script` | `ctx.tools` |
| `lsp-godot/` | GDScript navigation (`goToDefinition` / `findReferences`

/ `hover`) through Godot's built-in TCP language server, attach or spawn | `ctx.lsp` |
| `tool-godot
-debug/` | `godot_debug`: one bounded scripted debug run — breakpoints, headless launch, per-stop st

ack/variable snapshots, structured report | `ctx.tools` |
| `tool-godot-ego/` | Visual sandbox: a pe
rsistent running game the agent can see, read, and operate (`godot_play` plus 20 more tools) | `ctx.

tools` |
| `ui-godot/` | Web settings card for the `godot` namespace and the sandbox watch panel (fl
oating ball, live frame, click-to-drive) | browser slots |
The capabilities were migrated from **godot-vscode-plugin** (Godot Tools v2.7.1, ~700k installs), ke
eping the pure-logic cores; the migration is pinned by protocol facts recorded against a real Godot
4.7 instance. See docs/architecture.md for the module map and protocol-fact pointers.
## Prerequisites
- **Godot 4.2+.** The CLI tools and the debugger require a Godot 4.2 or newer build with `--headless

` support (spawn-mode LSP's version gate also accepts 3.6+).
- **Host binaries, resolved at call tim
e.** godot (and gdformat for the default `godot_format` backend) are host installs, never bundled; a
missing executable surfaces as the structured `GODOT_UNAVAILABLE` error at call time, never at load

time.
- **One-time project import.** Headless game mode does not auto-import; run `godot --headless

--editor --path <root> --import --quit` once per project, or expect a slower first run.
- **Writabl
e game user data.** The game's `user://` directory must be writable; game mode otherwise crashes wit
data.** The game's `user://` directory must be writable; game mode otherwise crashes with signal 11.
## Installation
Godot is **optional**: `dsh-base` and `dsh-web-app` mount none of these packages. The supported path
is the capability bundle, which inserts the five rows together and appears under **Installed plugin
s** in the Plugins page:

Restart `dsh web` after installing. The bundle's page carries the `tool-godot` settings form, and ev
ery row keeps the defaults listed under Configuration. A profile that wants only some rows can inser
t the individual packages instead and skip the bundle.
For an in-process or hand-written composition, mount the rows directly:

## Configuration
Every key has a default; per-package details live in each package's README.
| Package | Notable config | Defaults that matter |
| `tool-godot` | `executable`, `gdformatExecutable`, `formatBackend: 'gdformat' \| 'builtin'`, `time

outMs` | `executable: godot`; `timeoutMs: 60000` |
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
- **LSP.** Godot ships a TCP language server (EditorSettings `network/language_server/remote_port`,
default 6005). `lsp-godot` attaches to a running editor, or spawns a headless one (`--lsp-port`) and
pools providers per workspace; `.gd` queries (`goToDefinition` / `findReferences` / `hover`) are se

rved through the harness `ctx.lsp` seam.
- **Debugger.** Godot's remote debugger speaks a custom bin
ary protocol over `--remote-debug` — not DAP. Frames are `[u32 LE length][variant-encoded array]` of
`[command, threadId, params]` (Godot 4.2+). `godot_debug` binds a pre-picked free port, spawns the
game headless, snapshots the stack and locals/members/globals at each stop, and auto-continues up to

`maxStops`.
- **Visual sandbox.** A temporary `SceneTree` replaces the project's main loop and load
s a bridge from outside the project, so `project.godot` is never edited. The bridge answers newline-
delimited JSON over loopback (port and token travel through the environment), captures frames into m
emory, and injects input through `Viewport.push_input`. The game keeps running between calls; `godot

_see` delivers a frame into the conversation.
- **Scope.** `godot_debug` v1 is a launch-only scripte
d run that owns its game process; attach-mode debugging and stateful sessions are future work.
## Known limitations and deferred work
- Attach-mode debugging, dynamic breakpoints, scene-tree snapshots, multi-thread stops, lazy object

expansion and variable editing are future work (the pinned protocol facts keep those paths open).
-

The builtin formatter's whitespace rules follow godot-vscode-plugin, not gdformat.
- `godot_format`

is read-only by design; the model applies changes through the file-policy surface.
- Breakpoints nee

d a debug-capable binary; exported release builds may not deliver stops.
- A crashed harness can orp

han a spawned godot process.
- Variable rendering follows the source plugin's display precision (`to
Fixed(1)` math types, `toFixed(5)` floats).
